display.title: Episode 499: Reb Ariel and the Lion (Parshas Vayeira)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Vayeira show: Avraham Avinu's tent of kindness, Shema with a young guest, and the story of Reb Ariel, who kept Shabbos alone in the wilderness and was guarded by a lion.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Vayeira. Uncle Yossi explains the Alter Rebbe's teaching to 'live with the times', which the Mitteler Rebbe explained as living with the weekly sedra. In Vayeira, Avraham Avinu sets up his tent by the highway, feeds weary travelers and teaches them to thank Hashem instead of him, and children can do the same by helping a friend learn about Hashem. After the Hakochainik march, an eight-year-old girl from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: on Friday afternoon little Devorah helps her mother prepare for Shabbos and retells a story she heard at her class Shabbos party. Reb Ariel joins a caravan on condition that it rests on Shabbos, but the travelers break their word and leave him alone in the wilderness. A huge lion appears and guards him all Shabbos, then carries him on its back after Havdalah to the caravan, which had been attacked by wild animals. The travelers beg forgiveness and make him their teacher. The show closes with a listener's letter, how to write in, and candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Whoever guards Shabbos is guarded by Shabbos; and like Avraham Avinu, use kindness to bring others closer to Hashem.

date.note: 'The week of Vayeira'; candles 5:45, Shabbos ends 6:44: late Oct 1991 before the clock change. Fits the weekly run to episode 504 (Yud-Tes Kislev 5752).

advisories.note: A rabbi is left alone in a wilderness with wild animals; a huge lion approaches (it protects him); the caravan is attacked by wild beasts.

privacy.note: The Shema guest and a mailbox letter writer are named in full on air.

sources_cited.note: Explained by the Mitteler Rebbe as living with the weekly sedra.
